text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- IG Bau construction workers' union rejects arbitration ruling. Union offers to take part in negotiations but says it will be preparing to go on strike. Row over proposed cuts in sick pay. The union suggests compensation

- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) is opposed to proposed talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition government on reform of the pension system. Labour Minister Norbert Bluem accuses the SPD of being irresponsible
- It is still not certain whether Berlin's ruling grand coalition of Christian Democrats and Social Democrats will agree to the sale of Bewag facility
- Big penalties for more electricity cable companies involved in a price-fixing investigation

- Arne Boernsen is seen as favourite to become new government-appointed regulator for the telecommunications sector. Boernsen of the opposition SPD is currently chairman of a parliamentary committee on post and telecommunications
HANDELSBLATT
- Cable companies are ordered to pay fines by the Federal Cartel Office
- Growing danger of a strike in the construction sector after IG Bau building workers' union rejected an arbitration ruling
- Opposition Social Democrats reject talks on reforming the pension system with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition. Labour Minister Norbert Bluem is preparing a bill on pension reform
- Europe's largest pharmaceuticals company Gehe strives for new acquisitions and has set its sights on south east Asia and America
- Postbank posts shortfall of 1.2 billion marks in 1996
- Kohl dismisses speculation about new elections. He says elections will take place at the end of September to beginning of October next year
- German-Iranian relations continue to be strained. Tehran wants to protest to Bonn for sheltering Iranian opposition figures
- Berlin's SPD approves sale of Bewag electricity facility
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- IG Bau, construction union's pay talks commission rejects arbitration ruling. Construction sector stands on brink of battle for jobs. Union demands maintenance of full sick pay and threatens to go on strike if demands are not met. Employers reject IG Bau's revised offer. Employers fear bankrupcy in thousands of firms
- Opposition Social Democrats reject pension talks with ruling coalition
- Germany's 16 regional states support Bonn's savings plans. Cuts are planned in civil service
- Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU), sister party to Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), fears compromise over foreigners rights in Germany
- Germany's cartel office widened a price-fixing probe in the power cable industry to include several more groups after charging five firms with wrongdoing and issuing a hefty fines
- DIE WELT
- IG Bau construction workers' union rejects arbitration compromise. Union leader Klaus Wiesehuegel offers new pay talks. Employers decide today
- Opposition Social Democrats rejects talks on pension reform with coalition
- Genetic technology could combat malaria. Researchers look into new ways of combatting the disease
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl expects change in the jobs market trend
